## Abstract

<!--
Provide a short (< 100 words), high-level description of the data. Additional details can be provided in README file(s) accompanying the materials.
-->

The data analysis uses the Early Childhood Longitudinal Study, Kindergarten Class of 1998-99 (ECLS-K), Kindergarten-Eighth Grade public-use child file, released by the National Center for Education Statistics. The derived file `data_analysis/education.data.csv` (21,409 children, 21 variables) is an extract of that file. From it, the analysis forms 3 x 3 tables of primary nonparental care before kindergarten (center-based care, relative care, no nonparental care) by fall-kindergarten mathematics proficiency level (1-3) for Black girls (N = 94) and Black boys (N = 112) in low-income, single-parent families. All simulation data are generated by the code.

Column names and codes in `education.data.csv` are those of the ECLS-K public-use file (version 1.0). # Part 2: Code

## Abstract

<!--
Provide a short (< 100 words), high-level description of the code. Additional details can be provided in README file(s) accompanying the materials. If no code is provided, please state this and say why (e.g., if the paper contains no computational work).
-->

The `library/` folder implements the methods of the paper in R and C++ (`sensitivityIxJ.R`, `sensitivityIxJ.cpp`, `SIS_methods.cpp`): the exact worst-case p-value of ordinal, sign-score, and general count-based tests under the generic bias model, the sampling-based estimators, and the normal approximation based on the exact moments. The remaining folders hold the scripts that reproduce the results: the ECLS-K data analysis, the power and size simulations, the timing comparison of the kernel representation, the corner-solution counterexample, the running-time and memory benchmarks, and the verification scripts, together with the previous release of the engine kept for comparison.

R version 4.4.3 or later (the reported results were obtained with R version 4.6.1), with a C++ compiler for Rcpp. Optional, only to re-derive the profile-likelihood scores in the data analysis: Python 3.13.3 with Gurobi Optimizer 12.0.2 (a Gurobi license is required). R packages, with the versions used for the reported results: Rcpp 1.1.2 (all scripts), multicool 1.0.1, BiasedUrn 2.0.12, arrangements 1.1.10, sensitivitymv 1.4.4, dplyr 1.2.1, ggplot2 4.0.3, patchwork 1.3.2. ### Supporting system/hardware requirements (optional)

<!--
OPTIONAL: System/hardware requirements including operating system with version number, access to cluster, GPUs, etc.
-->

All results except the power simulations were obtained on Posit Cloud (Linux) with 8 CPUs and 4 GB RAM; no GPU is used. The power simulations were run on an HTCondor cluster, one job per (seed, gamma) pair, each job in an Apptainer/Singularity container with R (4.4 or later), Rcpp, and a C++ compiler, requesting 4 CPUs and 20 GB of memory; the same scripts also run on a single machine, as described in the README.

# Part 3: Reproducibility workflow

<!--
The materials provided should provide a straightforward way for reviewers and readers to reproduce analyses with as few steps as possible. 
-->

## Scope

The provided workflow reproduces:

- [x] Any numbers provided in text in the paper
- [x] The computational method(s) presented in the paper (i.e., code is provided that implements the method(s))
- [ ] All tables and figures in the paper
- [x] Selected tables and figures in the paper, as explained and justified below:

The workflow reproduces every table and figure that reports a computed quantity: the sensitivity-analysis tables of the data analysis (main text and Supplementary Material), the power tables, the size-control figures, the convergence figures of the sampling-based estimators, the computation-time tables, and the running-time and memory benchmarks. Three figures are illustrations (the introductory example of an I x J table, the collapsed and cross-cut tables, and the integer-to-dummy mapping) and involve no computation. The power-curve figures of the main text and the Supplementary Material plot the values of the power tables against gamma; each value is the total number of rejections written by the power scripts divided by 1,000. The Cross-Cut column of those tables (Fisher's exact test on the corner cells of the 3 x 3 table: treatment levels 1 and 3, outcome levels 1 and 3) is obtained from either 2 x 2 script by replacing the line that builds `observed.table` with `observed.table = matrix(c(n11, n13, n31, n33), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)`, as in the cross-cut tables of `data_analysis/education_data_analysis.R`; see README.txt, HOW TO REPRODUCE THE RESULTS, item 3. Computation times are reproduced up to the variation expected between machines; the chi-square benchmark for 3 x 4 tables is reported for N up to 120, and the entries marked X in that table were not computed.

### Instructions

<!--
Describe how to use the materials provided to reproduce analyses in the manuscript. For more complicated workflows, it is best to provide a short summary here with full  details  provided in README file(s) accompanying the reproducibility materials. If no workflow is provided, please state this and say why (e.g., if the paper contains no computational work).
-->

Full instructions are in `README.txt`, section HOW TO REPRODUCE THE RESULTS (items 1-9). In short: set the R working directory to the top-level folder of the repository (the one containing `README.txt`); every script begins by compiling and sourcing the library from `library/`, so no installation is needed. Each result is reproduced by sourcing one script by its path relative to the top-level folder: `data_analysis/education_data_analysis.R` (data analysis), `power_simulation/Kernel_Advantage_Simulation.R` (computation-time comparison and convergence figures), `power_simulation/size_control.R` (size control), `power_simulation/Corner_Solution_Counter_Example.R` (counterexample), and the scripts in `feasibility/` (benchmarks). The power simulations are run either on an HTCondor cluster (`condor_submit power_simulation/submit.txt`, then the shell script `command_generating_summary.txt` collects the rejection counts) or cell by cell on a single machine with `Rscript`, for which the README gives the command and its expected output. The scripts in `development_check/` verify the code and should all report PASS.

### Expected run-time

Approximate time needed to reproduce the analyses on a standard desktop machine:

- [ ] < 1 minute
- [ ] 1-10 minutes
- [ ] 10-60 minutes
- [ ] 1-8 hours
- [x] > 8 hours
- [ ] Not feasible to run on a desktop machine, as described here:

<!--
For more complicated situations, including cases where the run-time varies greatly across different analyses, more details can be provided in README file(s) that accompany the materials.
-->

The total is dominated by the two chi-square benchmarks over the full candidate set (about 4 hours for 3 x 3 tables and about 18 hours for 3 x 4 tables with N up to 120). Everything else runs in about 4 hours on a single machine: the data analysis, the counterexample, and the verification scripts take seconds to minutes; the size-control simulation about an hour; the computation-time comparison several minutes per table for the six tables of its first part, plus the sampling experiments of its second part; the ordinal benchmarks a few minutes; and the power simulations one to two minutes per (test, gamma) cell, 55 cells in all. Running times for each benchmark cell are reported in Section G of the Supplementary Material. All times were measured on Posit Cloud with 8 CPUs and 4 GB RAM and depend on the CPU and RAM available.

### Additional information (optional)

<!--
OPTIONAL: Additional documentation provided (e.g., R package vignettes, demos or other examples) that show how to use the provided code/software in other settings.
-->

The main functions in `library/sensitivityIxJ.R` are documented in the file (roxygen-style headers with arguments, returned values, and examples), and `README.txt` describes each function. The expected p-values of the data analysis are recorded as comments beside the corresponding calls in `education_data_analysis.R`. The scripts in `development_check/` show how the engine is checked against independent results (the multivariate hypergeometric distribution and `fisher.test()` at gamma = 0, total probability mass one, exact moments) and against the previous release in `legacy/`.

# Notes (optional)

<!--
OPTIONAL: Any other relevant information not covered on this form. 
-->

Random seeds are fixed in all scripts; the exact p-values involve no randomness and are reproduced to the printed precision on any platform. The `legacy/` folder contains the previous release of the engine and is used only by the verification script that compares the two engines. Author information was removed from the materials for review and will be restored in the public release.
